newsitem.title: USA: Columbus pays out $2.5 mln in bonuses.
newsitem.headline: Columbus pays out $2.5 mln in bonuses.

text.p: Columbus McKinnon Corp said Friday it paid out $2.5 million in bonuses to 2,000 of its employees.
The company said the bonus equaled 4.2 percent of the employees' pre-tax earnings in 1996.

Columbus has a separate executive incentive plan, said controller Karen Howard in an interview. She said coporate officers and plant managers receive a bonuses ranging from 30 percent of their annual base saleries to 45 percent if the company exceeds certain targets by more than 10 percent.
Howard said the executive bonuses are reduced by the company-wide 4.2 percent bonus. She added the plan is currently under revision.

Columbus posted a $18.4 milion net income, or $1.39 a share, in the fiscal year ended March 31, compared with a $13.0 million net, or $1.69 a share, the year before (both figures are excluding debt extinguishment). The company's stock traded at 19-1/8 Friday morning, down 1/8.
